To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Gale & Church's length-based statistical method can be applied successfully to the task of aligning English and Chinese sentences; (b) Gale & Church' method can be further improved by incorporating lexical cues; and (c) the HKUST English- Chinese Parallel Bilingual Corpus is an invaluable resource for research on Chinese language processing and for the study of bilingualism.

(1) our statistical method, which is based on the method of Gale & Church, is applicable to Chinese-English alignment; (2) our method can achieve an alignment accuracy of 90% on the HKUST corpus; (3) the accuracy of our method can be further improved to 95% by using a combination of lexical and statistical cues; and (4) we are currently in the process of expanding the HKUST corpus to 1 million words.
(1) the HKUST English- Chinese corpus is of sufficient size and quality for the alignment experiments, and (2) the lexical method outperforms the length-based method in the alignment task.
